active_paradigms.idea: Solve the true max-min distance formulation directly with constrained SLSQP rather than soft extrema plus random contact moves.
active_paradigms.description: The current program starts from the highly relevant rhombic-dodecahedral configuration (six axial and eight cubic vertices), then performs soft-min/soft-max gradient ascent and a long stochastic anneal over the nonsmooth exact ratio. Its strength is that this seed has the right broad symmetry and its active-set moves can escape one-coordinate traps, explaining the score near 0.991. Its principal weakness is that the soft surrogate changes the objective and its annealing has no mechanism to enforce all shortest and diameter constraints simultaneously at convergence. Parameterize 14 centered points, fixing translation by removing one coordinate block or adding centroid equalities, and add scalar t. Maximize t subject to every squared pair distance being at least t and at most 1; this is exactly the evaluator's squared ratio after scale normalization. Call scipy.optimize.minimize with method='SLSQP' once from the rhombic-dodecahedral seed, using analytic Jacobians for every pairwise constraint and the objective -t. Break rotational gauge freedom by fixing a few coordinates or use a very small quadratic gauge regularizer only on redundant degrees of freedom. Set ftol near 1e-12 and a large maxiter, then return the optimized coordinates scaled arbitrarily. This attacks the actual bottleneck: coordinated satisfaction of all active short and long contacts, rather than accepting transient noisy improvements in the ratio.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Directly maximize evaluator min_max_ratio = t under max squared distance normalized to 1; combined_score increases proportionally.
active_paradigms.cautions: SLSQP needs a feasible or nearly feasible starting point, so initially scale the seed to make its largest squared distance exactly 1 and initialize t slightly below its smallest squared distance. Supply constraints with the sign convention required by SLSQP and protect against finite-difference noise by providing analytic derivatives. Do not optimize a smoothed ratio; the scalar constrained epigraph form is materially better conditioned near tied contacts. Eliminate translation and preferably rotation gauges, otherwise the constraint Jacobian is rank-deficient and SLSQP may report misleading convergence.

active_paradigms.idea: Use a deterministic contact-graph rigidity solve with nonlinear least squares, based on the active edges identified in the rhombic-dodecahedral seed.
active_paradigms.description: The present search repeatedly discovers that only near-minimum and near-maximum pairs matter, but it samples which vertices to move rather than explicitly solving the contact equations. Extract the seed's two distance classes: candidate shortest contacts and candidate diameter contacts, and formulate residuals saying each short-contact squared distance equals t and each diameter-contact squared distance equals 1. Include centroid and orientation gauge residuals, and treat t as an additional unknown. Call scipy.optimize.least_squares on this single residual system with method='trf', tight tolerances, and an analytic sparse Jacobian whose rows touch only the two endpoints of each contact. A successful solve finds the locally rigid realization implied by the contact graph, which can reveal a symmetry-broken arrangement that the soft objective obscures. Select the contact graph from a narrowly perturbed best seed or from the exact seed, but retain only graphs for which the residual/Jacobian has the expected rank after gauge fixing. The resulting configuration should then be evaluated against all 91 pairs; its non-contact distances must remain strictly between t and 1. This is fundamentally different from random optimization because it exploits the likely fact that an optimum is characterized by a balanced, isostatic set of equal-distance constraints.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Equalize the genuinely binding minimum and maximum distance classes, reducing the slack and imbalance that leave the current score about 0.9% below the reference ratio.
active_paradigms.cautions: Least squares alone does not enforce inequalities for non-contact pairs, so reject a solved contact graph if any omitted pair becomes shorter than t or longer than 1. Avoid imposing every seed contact blindly: an overdetermined incompatible graph can lock the solution at the original symmetric point. Gauge constraints must remove exactly translation and rotation freedom without artificially fixing a meaningful deformation. The residuals should be in squared-distance units, consistent with the evaluator's squared objective.

active_paradigms.idea: Apply basin-hopping on the exact nonsmooth ratio with a geometry-aware coordinate parameterization and deterministic local acceptance.
active_paradigms.description: The current code is already an ad hoc annealer, but its local proposal radii are adapted from individual accept/reject events and its soft-ascent stage can enter a basin unrelated to the exact objective. Replace that custom stochastic process with scipy.optimize.basinhopping acting directly on negative min(q)/max(q), where q are all 91 squared distances. Use a centered 39-degree-of-freedom parameterization and normalize every proposed configuration by its current maximum squared distance, so the objective becomes simply the minimum squared distance and has no scale drift. Seed basin-hopping at several fixed, reproducible perturbations of the rhombic-dodecahedral arrangement, retaining the best result deterministically; the library call's local minimizer should work on the exact piecewise-smooth objective, not the current soft proxy. Supply a custom bounded random displacement that perturbs all vertices in a correlated low-rank mode as well as independent modes, because the current active-vertex-only moves can miss collective symmetry-breaking deformations. Use a low temperature and step size comparable to the observed contact-breaking scale, with a fixed seed and enough iterations to cross narrow ridges. The notable improvement opportunity is objective fidelity: every accept/reject and local descent decision is judged by precisely the score evaluated externally. Unlike constrained SLSQP, this method is specifically intended to search competing contact graphs and can find a better basin before final exact local settling.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Escape the current rhombic-dodecahedral contact basin while optimizing only the exact squared distance ratio used in combined_score.
active_paradigms.cautions: The default local minimizer is poorly suited to raw min/max kinks; use a local method tolerant of finite differences and ensure normalization is performed inside the objective without mutating the optimizer's input. Translation must be removed after each proposal, and a degenerate point set must return a large finite penalty rather than NaN. Basin-hopping can be expensive, so use fixed seeds and a modest number of well-scaled runs rather than the current extremely long two-level random loop. It is a global search method, not a proof of optimality; always preserve the unperturbed symmetric seed as a fallback.
